faq.question: How is usage calculated?
faq.answer: Topaz Video AI charges for source duration, first rounded up to whole seconds and then to whole billing steps. The chosen model and output tier set the step length; interpolation also depends on frame rate and slow-motion factor. Even a short clip consumes at least one step. The displayed per-second rate is the step price divided by its length. Acceptance holds the measured upload duration or the maximum linked-clip duration; unused funds return after actual usage is known, and failed jobs incur no charge. Within Topaz Video AI enlargement, the presets share a rate at a given tier except `gaia_2_animation`, which has its own pricing. Higher tiers cost more. Nyx Fast is priced below Nyx, and Hyperion 1 below Hyperion 2.5. Higher interpolation frame rates and slowing factors increase the work; Aion has the highest interpolation rate.

faq.question: What happens to the audio?
faq.answer: Enhancement and ordinary frame-rate conversion keep the sound; the tested slowed clips omit it, so a slow-motion edit needs its own audio treatment.

faq.question: How do I choose the settings?
faq.answer: Use Proteus for a general enlargement trial, Nyx for grain or Apollo for retiming; specialize only after inspecting the defect in the source.

useCases.title: Put the clip to work
useCases.body: Prepare an old phone recording or an interview excerpt for a larger edit. Pick an enlargement preset suited to the source, then check skin, hair and compression marks before using the result in the final timeline.

useCases.title: Inspect the result
useCases.body: Work on a dim interior, a blurred dance shot or a movement study with the matching tool. Keep noise treatment, HDR conversion and slow motion as deliberate choices so you can assess each result against its source.

limits.body: Enlargement can leave compressed patches visible; a higher tier does not certify recovered source detail, and the two fixed-2× presets need a dimension check.

Denoise, Deblur & HDR processes the clip at the requested resolution. Start with `nyx` for natural-looking noise treatment, or choose `deblur` for softness. Hyperion outputs HEVC (H.265), 10-bit HDR; browser previews may fail, so review the download in an HDR-capable player or editor. Other presets output H.264. The tested Hyperion 2.5 file is tagged PQ (`smpte2084`), while the Hyperion 1 sample is tagged HLG (`arib-std-b67`); check the returned file’s HDR metadata in your player or editor.

Input is read at 30 fps for frame interpolation. With `slow_motion` above `1`, duration increases and the tested output has no audio; ordinary enhancement and frame conversion without slowing retain the soundtrack.

familyContent.closing: Trim to a useful passage of 1–60 seconds and send its MP4 through `video_url`. Start with `1080p` and the default preset for the chosen tool, keeping an untouched copy for review. A higher delivery tier cannot guarantee recovery of detail missing from the recording. Watch the full clip after processing, especially hands in motion and edges against busy backgrounds. For HDR, download the file to a compatible player or editor. For slow motion, plan a separate sound edit because the tested slowed outputs contain no audio track.

data.description: Use the enlargement endpoint when the main task is fitting an existing shot into a larger frame. The output keeps the scene’s timing and sound, while the selected model determines how edges and damaged detail are treated.

paramNotes.preset:
- `proteus` — general default
- `proteus_natural` — natural enhancement, always 2×
- `rhea` — high-fidelity detail enlargement
- `artemis_hq` — high-quality source
- `artemis_mq` — medium-quality source
- `artemis_lq` — low-quality source
- `artemis_medium_halo` — moderate edge halos
- `artemis_strong_halo` — strong edge halos
- `artemis_aliasing_moire` — aliasing and moiré
- `gaia_hq` — add detail to clean footage
- `gaia_cg` — animation and CG
- `gaia_2_animation` — animation, always 2×
- `theia_detail` — strong frame-by-frame detail
- `theia_fidelity` — consistent fidelity
- `iris_mq` — moderately degraded faces
- `iris_lq` — severely degraded faces
- `dione_dv` — DV interlacing
- `dione_tv` — TV interlacing
- `dione_robust` — difficult interlacing
- `dione_dehalo` — interlacing with halo removal
- `dione_robust_dehalo` — difficult interlacing with halo removal

Default: `proteus`. At the same tier, all presets except `gaia_2_animation` have the same rate.
paramNotes.resolution: Choose `720p`, `1080p` (default), `2k` or `4k`; higher tiers increase cost while preserving aspect ratio. `proteus_natural` and `gaia_2_animation` use fixed 2× enlargement instead of normal tier sizing.
paramNotes.video_url: Required MP4 URL or upload, 1–60 seconds; longer or shorter sources are rejected before acceptance. Enlargement retains the source duration and audio track.

preset.description: Which Topaz Video AI enhancement model to run (Proteus, Rhea, Artemis, Gaia, Theia, Iris or Dione). Sets the per-second rate together with resolution.

resolution.description: Output tier; the clip's aspect ratio is kept. Proteus Natural and Gaia 2 Animation always enlarge 2x. Sets the per-second rate.

video_url.description: The clip to process, 1 to 60 seconds long, as an MP4 link or upload. Length and audio are kept; clips outside that range are rejected before any charge.

data.pricingNote: Upscale usage depends on the selected model and resolution tier. Source duration is rounded up to a whole second, then to a full billing step, with one step as the minimum. The displayed second rate equals the step price divided by step length. Acceptance reserves the measured upload duration or 60 seconds for a URL; completion releases the excess and failures cost nothing. Twenty presets share a tier rate; `gaia_2_animation` is priced separately, and larger tiers cost more.
data.readme:
## Introduction

Video AI’s enlargement tool is for a small recording that needs a larger place in an edit: an interview insert, a phone clip or an animated scene. It offers source-specific processing rather than a single look, so a face-damaged transfer and a clean computer-rendered shot need not receive the same treatment.

## Key features & Highlights

The 21-model selection covers general enhancement, several degrees of source damage, edge halos, repeating interference and interlacing. Proteus provides the initial setting, Rhea focuses on faithful detail, and Iris addresses faces in degraded material. Dione is relevant when alternating scan lines are part of the recording rather than ordinary blur.

The podcast trial expanded a five-second 640×360 shot into a 1920×1080 file without losing its microphone audio or 24 fps timing. In the street trial, bicycle contours became easier to read but block-shaped compression remained in places. The result demonstrates useful enlargement while leaving a visible ceiling on what the damaged input can support.

## Use cases

For a talking-head compilation, process a short answer that includes both facial movement and the microphone. This exposes problems that a still portrait would conceal, including edges that change as the speaker turns.

For a mixed-media sequence, separate animation from old DV material before testing. Gaia’s animation options and Dione’s interlace treatments address different source structures; one choice across the entire sequence can miss the reason a particular shot looks poor.

## Prompt guide & Pro tips

There is no prompt field for this operation. Start with `proteus` at `1080p`, inspect a representative section and change the model according to the visible problem. Moving directly to 4K increases the delivery size and cost without establishing that the selected model suits the source.

Check the returned dimensions before conforming the shot, especially with the two presets that always double width and height. Compare thin lines, eyes and hair at the intended display size, then play the whole take with sound. Keep the input beside the output during approval so sharper contours are not mistaken for complete removal of compressed texture.
